title: Ch 6 · Model of Cells - The Basic Units of Life

questions.q: What are the basic building blocks of all living things?
questions.explain: Cells are the basic units of life. All living things are made up of one or more cells.
questions.lo: State that cells are the basic units of life and need a microscope to be seen

notes.0: Organs are made of tissues, which are made of cells, so organs are not the smallest unit. Think about what organs are built from at the smallest level.
notes.2: A tissue is a group of similar cells working together, so it is built from smaller units. Think about what tissues are made of.
notes.3: A system is made of several organs working together, so it is a large unit, not a building block. Think about the smallest unit of life.

questions.q: Why do we need a microscope to study cells?
choices: most cells are too small to see
cells only exist inside the body
questions.explain: Most cells are too small to be seen with the naked eye. A microscope magnifies them so that the cells and their parts can be seen.
questions.lo: State that cells are the basic units of life and need a microscope to be seen

notes.1: Cells are found in all living things, including plants and unicellular organisms, not only inside the body. Think about the size of a cell.
notes.2: Many cells, such as plant cells, do not move at all, yet they still need a microscope to be seen. Think about the size of a cell.
notes.3: Many cells are not transparent, such as green plant cells. Think about why a cell cannot be seen even when it is coloured.

why.right: A microscope makes small objects look larger, so the details of tiny cells can be seen.
wrong: A microscope makes cells move more slowly, so the details of fast cells can be seen.
A microscope adds colour to clear objects, so the details of transparent cells can be seen.

questions.q: What does a light microscope use to magnify images?
questions.explain: A light microscope passes visible light through the specimen and uses glass lenses to magnify the image.
questions.lo: Relate advances in microscope technology to knowledge about cells

notes.0: Sound waves are not used to form images in a light microscope. The name of the microscope gives a clue to what it uses.
notes.1: A light microscope may have a mirror to direct light onto the specimen, but a mirror alone does not magnify. Think about which part makes the image larger.
notes.3: Electrons and magnets are used in an electron microscope. A light microscope works in a different way, as its name suggests.

questions.q: Which microscope shows more detail of a cell?
questions.explain: An electron microscope can magnify far more than a light microscope, so it shows much finer detail inside a cell.
questions.lo: Relate advances in microscope technology to knowledge about cells

notes.0: A telescope is used to look at distant objects, such as stars, not tiny objects close by. Think about instruments built to magnify cells.
notes.1: A hand lens magnifies only a few times, which is not enough to see inside a cell. Think about the instrument with the greatest magnification.
notes.2: A light microscope can show cells and some of their parts, but its magnification is limited. Think about a more powerful type of microscope.

why.right: An electron microscope shows more detail because it can magnify far more than a light microscope.
wrong: An electron microscope shows more detail because it uses brighter visible light than a light microscope.
An electron microscope shows more detail because it makes the cells themselves grow larger.

questions.q: Small structures in a cell could not be seen until microscopes improved. This shows that
choices: cells did not have these structures before
advances in technology help build scientific knowledge
questions.explain: The structures were always in cells, but they could not be seen until microscopes improved. Better technology let scientists build new knowledge about cells.
questions.lo: Relate advances in microscope technology to knowledge about cells

notes.0: Knowledge about cells did change once the small structures were seen. Think about what made it possible to see them.
notes.1: The structures were there all along. They were not seen earlier because the microscopes of the time could not show them.
notes.3: Small structures in cells carry out important jobs. Think about what made it possible to see them for the first time.

why.right: Scientists could describe the small structures only after microscopes could magnify them enough.
wrong: Scientists could describe the small structures only after cells grew these structures over time.
Scientists could describe the small structures only after deciding that larger structures did not matter.

questions.q: What is the function of the cell membrane?
choices: controls what enters and leaves the cell
gives the cell a regular shape
questions.explain: The cell membrane is a thin layer around the cell. It controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.
questions.lo: State the function of each part of a typical cell

notes.0: Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts, not the cell membrane. Think about the job of the thin layer around the cell.
notes.2: A regular shape is given by the cell wall in plant cells. The cell membrane is a thin layer with a different job.
notes.3: Storing liquids, food and waste is the job of the vacuole. The cell membrane is a thin outer layer with a different job.

questions.q: What is the function of the cell wall?
choices: controls all activities of the cell
questions.explain: The cell wall is a tough, rigid layer outside the cell membrane of a plant cell. It protects and supports the cell and gives it a regular shape.
questions.lo: State the function of each part of a typical cell

notes.1: Controlling all the activities of the cell is the job of the nucleus. The cell wall is a tough outer layer with a different job.
notes.2: Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts. The cell wall is a tough outer layer with a different job.
notes.3: Storing liquids, food and waste is the job of the vacuole. The cell wall is a tough outer layer with a different job.

questions.q: What is the function of the nucleus?
choices: controls all activities of the cell
questions.explain: The nucleus controls all the activities of the cell. It also contains DNA, the genetic material.
questions.lo: State the function of each part of a typical cell

notes.0: Most chemical reactions take place in the cytoplasm. The nucleus contains DNA, so think about what that lets it do.
notes.1: Storing liquids, food and waste is the job of the vacuole. The nucleus contains DNA, so think about what that lets it do.
notes.2: Protecting and supporting the cell is the job of the cell wall. The nucleus contains DNA, so think about what that lets it do.

questions.q: What is the function of the chloroplast?
choices: controls all activities of the cell
questions.explain: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light. Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts.
questions.lo: State the function of each part of a typical cell

notes.0: Storing liquids, food and waste is the job of the vacuole. Chloroplasts contain the green pigment chlorophyll, so think about what that is used for.
notes.1: Controlling all the activities of the cell is the job of the nucleus. Chloroplasts contain the green pigment chlorophyll, so think about what that is used for.
notes.3: Protecting and supporting the cell is the job of the cell wall. Chloroplasts contain the green pigment chlorophyll, so think about what that is used for.

questions.q: What is the function of the vacuole?
choices: stores liquids, food and waste materials
controls all activities of the cell
questions.explain: The vacuole is a space in the cell filled with fluid. It stores liquids, food and waste materials.
questions.lo: State the function of each part of a typical cell

notes.0: Most chemical reactions take place in the cytoplasm. The vacuole is a fluid-filled space, so think about what it might hold.
notes.2: Controlling all the activities of the cell is the job of the nucleus. The vacuole is a fluid-filled space, so think about what it might hold.
notes.3: Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts. The vacuole is a fluid-filled space, so think about what it might hold.

questions.q: What is the function of the cytoplasm?
choices: controls all activities of the cell
site where most chemical reactions take place
questions.explain: The cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance that fills the cell. Most of the chemical reactions of the cell take place in it.
questions.lo: State the function of each part of a typical cell

notes.0: Storing liquids, food and waste is the job of the vacuole. Think about what happens in the jelly-like substance that fills the cell.
notes.1: Controlling all the activities of the cell is the job of the nucleus. Think about what happens in the jelly-like substance that fills the cell.
notes.2: Protecting and supporting the cell is the job of the cell wall. Think about what happens in the jelly-like substance that fills the cell.

questions.q: A jelly-like substance fills the cell. Which part is this?
questions.explain: The cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance that fills the cell. The other cell parts are found in it.
questions.lo: Identify a cell part from a description of its function

notes.1: The vacuole is a fluid-filled space held inside the cell. Think about the substance that surrounds the vacuole and the other parts.
notes.2: The cell membrane is a thin layer around the cell, not a substance that fills it. Think about what lies inside the membrane.
notes.3: The nucleus is one part inside the cell that controls its activities. Think about the substance that surrounds the nucleus.

questions.q: A tough, rigid layer gives a plant cell its regular shape. Which part is this?
questions.explain: The cell wall is a tough, rigid layer around a plant cell. It gives the cell a regular shape and supports it.
questions.lo: Identify a cell part from a description of its function

notes.0: Chloroplasts are small structures where photosynthesis takes place. They do not form a layer around the cell.
notes.1: The cytoplasm is jelly-like, so it cannot hold the cell in a fixed shape. Think about the tough outer layer of a plant cell.
notes.2: The cell membrane is thin and flexible, so it does not give a fixed shape. Think about the layer outside it in a plant cell.

questions.q: A thin layer lies just below the cell wall. Which part is this?
questions.explain: The cell membrane is a thin layer found just inside the cell wall of a plant cell.
questions.lo: Identify a cell part from a description of its function

notes.1: The cytoplasm is a jelly-like substance, not a thin layer. It lies further inside the cell.
notes.2: The nucleus is a rounded structure inside the cell, not a layer. Think about what lies just inside the cell wall.
notes.3: The vacuole is a fluid-filled space in the cell, not a thin layer. Think about what lies just inside the cell wall.

questions.q: A cell part is called the "food factory" of a plant cell. Which part is this?
questions.explain: Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts, where the plant makes its own food. So the chloroplast is called the food factory of a plant cell.
questions.lo: Identify a cell part from a description of its function

notes.0: Many chemical reactions happen in the cytoplasm, but it does not make food using light. Think about where photosynthesis takes place.
notes.1: The vacuole stores food, but it does not make food. Think about where photosynthesis takes place.
notes.3: The nucleus controls the activities of the cell, but it does not make food itself. Think about where photosynthesis takes place.

why.right: Chloroplasts are called food factories because photosynthesis, which makes food, takes place in them.
wrong: Chloroplasts are called food factories because they store the food that the cell takes in.
Chloroplasts are called food factories because they break down food to release waste.

questions.q: A cell dies when one part is removed. Which part was removed?
questions.explain: The nucleus controls all the activities of the cell. Without it, the cell cannot carry out its life processes and it dies.
questions.lo: Identify a cell part from a description of its function

notes.0: Many plant cells, such as root cells, live with no chloroplasts at all. Think about the part that controls the activities of the cell.
notes.2: Animal cells have no cell wall and still live. Think about the part that controls the activities of the cell.
notes.3: A vacuole stores substances, so losing it is not what kills the cell. Think about the part that controls the activities of the cell.

why.right: A cell dies without its nucleus because the nucleus controls all the activities of the cell.
wrong: A cell dies without its nucleus because the nucleus makes all the food the cell needs.
A cell dies without its nucleus because the nucleus holds the cell in its shape.

questions.q: The chloroplasts in a leaf cell are damaged. Which process stops in that cell?
choices: movement of substances into the cell
questions.explain: Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts. If the chloroplasts are damaged, the cell can no longer carry out photosynthesis.
questions.lo: Identify a cell part from a description of its function

notes.0: Movement of substances into the cell is controlled by the cell membrane. Think about what chloroplasts do in a leaf cell.
notes.1: Support comes from the cell wall. Think about what chloroplasts do in a leaf cell.
notes.3: Storage of waste happens in the vacuole. Think about what chloroplasts do in a leaf cell.

why.right: Photosynthesis stops because chloroplasts contain the chlorophyll that absorbs light energy.
wrong: Photosynthesis stops because chloroplasts carry the water into the leaf cell.
Photosynthesis stops because chloroplasts hold the leaf cell in a fixed shape.

questions.q: Which part of the cell contains DNA?
questions.explain: The nucleus contains DNA, the genetic material of the cell.
questions.lo: State that the nucleus contains DNA, the genetic material passed to offspring

notes.1: The vacuole stores liquids, food and waste, not genetic material. Think about the part that controls the cell.
notes.2: The cytoplasm is where most chemical reactions take place. The genetic material is kept inside a separate structure.
notes.3: The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell. The genetic material is kept inside a separate structure.

questions.q: DNA is the genetic material that is
choices: used to store food and waste
used to make food by photosynthesis
passed down from parents to offspring
questions.explain: DNA is the genetic material in the nucleus. It is passed down from parents to their offspring.
questions.lo: State that the nucleus contains DNA, the genetic material passed to offspring

notes.0: Storing food and waste is the job of the vacuole. DNA carries information, so think about how features are passed on in families.
notes.1: Making food by photosynthesis happens in chloroplasts. DNA carries information, so think about how features are passed on in families.
notes.2: DNA is found in the cells of animals as well as plants. Think about how features are passed on in families.

questions.q: Where is a cell wall found?
choices: in both plant and animal cells
questions.explain: A cell wall is found in plant cells only. Animal cells have a cell membrane but no cell wall.
questions.lo: Classify cell parts as found in plant cells only or in both

notes.0: Animal cells have no cell wall. Their outer layer is the cell membrane. Think about which cells have a rigid, regular shape.
notes.2: Animal cells have only a cell membrane on the outside. Think about which cells have a tough, rigid layer as well.

questions.q: Where is a nucleus found?
choices: in both plant and animal cells
questions.explain: A typical plant cell and a typical animal cell both have a nucleus to control their activities.
questions.lo: Classify cell parts as found in plant cells only or in both

notes.0: Plant cells need a part to control their activities too. Think about whether a typical plant cell has a nucleus.
notes.1: Animal cells need a part to control their activities too. Think about whether a typical animal cell has a nucleus.

questions.q: Where are chloroplasts found?
choices: in both plant and animal cells
questions.explain: Chloroplasts are found in plant cells only. Animals do not carry out photosynthesis, so animal cells have no chloroplasts.
questions.lo: Classify cell parts as found in plant cells only or in both

notes.0: Animal cells do not carry out photosynthesis. Think about which living things make their own food.
notes.2: Animals get food by eating, not by photosynthesis. Think about which living things make their own food.

why.right: Plant cells have chloroplasts because plants make their own food by photosynthesis, and animals do not.
wrong: Plant cells have chloroplasts because plants need energy to live, and animals do not.
Plant cells have chloroplasts because plants have a cell wall to protect them, and animals do not.

questions.q: Where is a cell membrane found?
choices: in both plant and animal cells
questions.explain: Both plant and animal cells have a cell membrane that controls what enters and leaves the cell.
questions.lo: Classify cell parts as found in plant cells only or in both

notes.1: Animal cells also need to control what enters and leaves them. Think about whether animal cells have a cell membrane.
notes.2: Plant cells also need to control what enters and leaves them. In a plant cell, this layer lies just inside the cell wall.

questions.q: Where is cytoplasm found?
choices: in both plant and animal cells
questions.explain: Both plant and animal cells contain cytoplasm, where most chemical reactions take place.
questions.lo: Classify cell parts as found in plant cells only or in both

notes.0: Plant cells also carry out chemical reactions to stay alive. Think about whether a plant cell is filled with cytoplasm.
notes.2: Animal cells also carry out chemical reactions to stay alive. Think about whether an animal cell is filled with cytoplasm.

questions.q: Which is NOT a difference between a plant and an animal cell?
choices: presence of a large central vacuole
questions.explain: Both plant and animal cells have a cell membrane, so it is not a difference between them. The cell wall, chloroplasts and large central vacuole are found in plant cells only.
questions.lo: Classify cell parts as found in plant cells only or in both

notes.0: A cell wall is found in plant cells but not in animal cells, so it is a difference. Look for a part that both cells share.
notes.1: Chloroplasts are found in plant cells but not in animal cells, so they are a difference. Look for a part that both cells share.
notes.2: A large central vacuole is found in plant cells, while animal cells have small vacuoles. So it is a difference. Look for a part that both share.

why.right: A cell membrane is not a difference because both plant and animal cells have one.
wrong: A cell membrane is not a difference because neither plant nor animal cells have one.
A cell membrane is not a difference because it is part of the cell wall in both cells.

questions.q: What are the vacuoles like in a typical plant cell?
questions.explain: A typical plant cell has one large central vacuole, or sometimes two, filled with cell sap.
questions.lo: Compare the vacuoles and size of typical plant and animal cells

notes.0: Many small vacuoles are found in a typical animal cell. A plant cell vacuole takes up much of the cell.
notes.1: A plant cell vacuole is not small. It often takes up most of the space inside the cell.
notes.2: Plant cells do have vacuoles. Think about how much of the cell the vacuole fills.

questions.q: What are the vacuoles like in a typical animal cell?
questions.explain: A typical animal cell has many small vacuoles. A typical plant cell has one large central vacuole instead.
questions.lo: Compare the vacuoles and size of typical plant and animal cells

notes.1: A typical animal cell does have vacuoles. Think about their size and number compared with a plant cell.
notes.2: One or two large vacuoles are found in a typical plant cell. Animal cell vacuoles are different in size and number.
notes.3: A large central vacuole is a feature of plant cells. Animal cell vacuoles are different in size and number.

questions.q: A typical cell model shows what cells
questions.explain: A typical cell model shows the parts that most cells of that type have. Real cells can differ from it.
questions.lo: Show that typical plant and animal cells are models of many cell forms

notes.0: A model shows parts that cells do have, not parts they lack. Think about how many real cells match the model.
notes.1: A model shows parts that cells do have, and real cells can have them. Think about how many real cells match the model.
notes.3: Some real cells lack parts shown in the model, such as a red blood cell with no nucleus. So the model is not true for every cell.

why.right: A typical cell model shows the common features of many cells, but real cells can differ from it.
wrong: A typical cell model shows the features found in every cell, and real cells never differ from it.
A typical cell model shows features found in no real cell, so it is only imaginary.

questions.q: A red blood cell has no nucleus. What does this show about typical cell models?
choices: the nucleus is not needed by any cell
red blood cells are not animal cells
real cells can differ from the model
questions.explain: A red blood cell is a real animal cell that has no nucleus. This shows that real cells can differ from the typical cell model.
questions.lo: Show that typical plant and animal cells are models of many cell forms

notes.0: Most cells need a nucleus to control their activities. One cell without a nucleus does not show that no cell needs one.
notes.1: A red blood cell is an animal cell found in human blood. Think about how it compares with the typical model.
notes.3: The model is still useful because it shows what most animal cells have. Think about what one unusual cell shows about the model.

why.right: A typical cell model shows the features most cells have, so some real cells will not match it.
wrong: A typical cell model shows the features all cells have, so a cell without a nucleus must be dead.
A typical cell model shows the features of plant cells only, so animal cells will not match it.

questions.q: A root hair cell has no chloroplasts. Which statement is correct?
choices: it is still a plant cell
it must be an animal cell
it cannot be a living cell
questions.explain: Root hair cells are underground, where there is no light for photosynthesis, so they have no chloroplasts. They are still plant cells with a cell wall.
questions.lo: Show that typical plant and animal cells are models of many cell forms

notes.1: A root hair cell is one of many cells in a plant, not a whole organism on its own. Think about where it is found.
notes.2: Not every plant cell has chloroplasts. Look at the other parts of a root hair cell, such as its outer layer.
notes.3: A cell can be alive without chloroplasts, as animal cells show. Think about what kind of organism the root belongs to.

why.right: A root hair cell is a plant cell because it has a cell wall, even though it has no chloroplasts.
wrong: A root hair cell is a plant cell because all cells found in the soil are plant cells.
A root hair cell is a plant cell because only plant cells can live without chloroplasts.

questions.q: A cell has a cell wall, a nucleus and no chloroplasts. It is from
choices: an animal, because it has no chloroplasts
a plant, because it has a cell wall
an animal, because it has a nucleus
a plant, because it has a nucleus
questions.explain: Only plant cells have a cell wall, so the cell is from a plant. Some plant cells, such as root cells, have no chloroplasts.
questions.lo: Infer whether a cell is from a plant or an animal from its structures

notes.0: Some plant cells, such as root cells, have no chloroplasts. Look for a part in this cell that animal cells never have.
notes.2: Both plant and animal cells have a nucleus, so it cannot show which one this is. Look for a part that animal cells never have.
notes.3: Both plant and animal cells have a nucleus, so it cannot show which one this is. Look for a part that only one kind of cell has.

why.right: A cell wall is found only in plant cells, so it shows the cell comes from a plant.
wrong: A nucleus is found only in plant cells, so it shows the cell comes from a plant.
Chloroplasts are found in every plant cell, so their absence shows the cell comes from an animal.

questions.q: A cell stores oil and has a nucleus but no cell wall. It is from
choices: a plant, because it has a nucleus
an animal, because it has a nucleus
a plant, because it stores oil
an animal, because it has no cell wall
questions.explain: Every plant cell has a cell wall. This cell has no cell wall, so it is from an animal. Storing oil and having a nucleus do not decide this.
questions.lo: Infer whether a cell is from a plant or an animal from its structures

notes.0: Both plant and animal cells have a nucleus, so it cannot show which one this is. Look at the part this cell is missing.
notes.1: Animal cells do have a nucleus, but so do plant cells. Look for a reason that fits only one kind of cell.
notes.2: Both plant and animal cells can store oil, so it cannot show which one this is. Look at the part this cell is missing.

why.right: A cell with no cell wall cannot be a plant cell, because every plant cell has a cell wall.
wrong: A cell that stores oil cannot be a plant cell, because plant cells store only starch.
A cell with a nucleus cannot be a plant cell, because plant cells have no nucleus.

questions.q: A cell has chloroplasts, a cell wall and a large vacuole. It is from
choices: a plant, because it has chloroplasts
a plant, because it has a nucleus
an animal, because it has a vacuole
an animal, because it has a membrane
questions.explain: Chloroplasts, a cell wall and a large vacuole are all found in plant cells only. Chloroplasts alone are enough to show the cell is from a plant.
questions.lo: Infer whether a cell is from a plant or an animal from its structures

notes.1: The cell is from a plant, but a nucleus is not the reason. Both plant and animal cells have a nucleus.
notes.2: Animal cells have only small vacuoles. A large vacuole, a cell wall and chloroplasts all point to one kind of cell.
notes.3: Both plant and animal cells have a membrane, so it cannot show which one this is. Look for parts that only one kind of cell has.

why.right: Chloroplasts are found only in plant cells, so they show the cell comes from a plant.
wrong: Vacuoles are found only in plant cells, so they show the cell comes from a plant.
Cell membranes are found only in plant cells, so they show the cell comes from a plant.

questions.q: A cell has no nucleus, no cell wall and no chloroplasts. It is from
choices: a plant, because it has no chloroplasts
a plant, because it has no nucleus
an animal, because it has no cell wall
an animal, because it has no nucleus
questions.explain: Every plant cell has a cell wall. This cell has no cell wall, so it is from an animal. A red blood cell is an example.
questions.lo: Infer whether a cell is from a plant or an animal from its structures

notes.0: Having no chloroplasts does not point to a plant. Look at which missing part every plant cell would need to have.
notes.1: Having no nucleus does not point to a plant. Look at which missing part every plant cell would need to have.
notes.3: Most animal cells do have a nucleus, so a missing nucleus does not show it is an animal cell. Look at which missing part every plant cell has.

why.right: A cell with no cell wall must be an animal cell, because every plant cell has a cell wall.
wrong: A cell with no nucleus must be an animal cell, because every plant cell has a nucleus.
A cell with no chloroplasts must be an animal cell, because every plant cell has chloroplasts.

questions.q: A cell has many small vacuoles and no cell wall. It is from
choices: a plant, because it has many vacuoles
an animal, because it has vacuoles
a plant, because it has vacuoles
an animal, because it has no cell wall
questions.explain: Every plant cell has a cell wall, so a cell with no cell wall is from an animal. Many small vacuoles are also typical of animal cells.
questions.lo: Infer whether a cell is from a plant or an animal from its structures

notes.0: Many small vacuoles are typical of animal cells. Plant cells usually have one or two large vacuoles.
notes.1: Plant cells have vacuoles too, so having vacuoles does not show it is an animal cell. Look at the part this cell is missing.
notes.2: Both plant and animal cells have vacuoles, so having vacuoles cannot decide this. Look at the part this cell is missing.

why.right: Plant cells always have a cell wall, so a cell without one comes from an animal.
wrong: Plant cells never have vacuoles, so a cell with vacuoles comes from an animal.
Plant cells always have chloroplasts, so a cell without them comes from an animal.

questions.q: Which observation shows that an unknown cell comes from a plant?
questions.explain: A cell wall is found in plant cells but not in animal cells. Cytoplasm, a cell membrane and a nucleus are found in both.
questions.lo: Infer whether a cell is from a plant or an animal from its structures

notes.0: Cytoplasm is found in both plant and animal cells, so it cannot show which one this is. Look for a part only plant cells have.
notes.2: A cell membrane is found in both plant and animal cells, so it cannot show which one this is. Look for a part only plant cells have.
notes.3: A nucleus is found in both plant and animal cells, so it cannot show which one this is. Look for a part only plant cells have.

why.right: A cell wall shows a plant cell because animal cells do not have one.
wrong: A cell wall shows a plant cell because only plant cells need protection.
A cell wall shows a plant cell because it is where photosynthesis takes place.

questions.q: A cell was inferred to be from an animal. Which part did it lack?
questions.explain: Every plant cell has a cell wall. A cell without a cell wall can be inferred to be from an animal.
questions.lo: Infer whether a cell is from a plant or an animal from its structures

notes.0: Most animal cells have a nucleus, and so do plant cells. A missing nucleus cannot show that a cell is from an animal.
notes.2: Every cell, plant or animal, has a cell membrane. Look for a part that animal cells lack but plant cells have.
notes.3: Every cell, plant or animal, contains cytoplasm. Look for a part that animal cells lack but plant cells have.

why.right: A missing cell wall shows an animal cell because every plant cell has a cell wall.
wrong: A missing nucleus shows an animal cell because every plant cell has a nucleus.
A missing cytoplasm shows an animal cell because every plant cell is filled with cytoplasm.

questions.q: A unicellular organism is made up of
questions.explain: A unicellular organism is made up of only one cell. That one cell carries out all the life processes.
questions.lo: Classify organisms as unicellular or multicellular

notes.0: An organism with many cells, even similar ones, is multicellular. Think about what the prefix uni means.
notes.1: Tissues and organs are made of many cells, so they are found in multicellular organisms. Think about what the prefix uni means.
notes.2: Many types of cells are found in multicellular organisms. Think about what the prefix uni means.

questions.q: Which organism is unicellular?
questions.explain: A bacterium is made up of only one cell, so it is unicellular. A mushroom, a worm and a cat are made up of many cells.
questions.lo: Classify organisms as unicellular or multicellular

notes.1: A mushroom is made up of a great many cells, so it is multicellular. Look for an organism whose whole body is one cell.
notes.2: Even a small worm has many cells, so it is multicellular. Look for an organism whose whole body is one cell.
notes.3: A cat has a huge number of cells forming tissues and organs. Look for an organism whose whole body is one cell.

why.right: A bacterium is unicellular because its whole body is made up of only one cell.
wrong: A bacterium is unicellular because it is too small to be seen without a microscope.
A bacterium is unicellular because it lives in water and in soil.

questions.q: Which organism is multicellular?
questions.explain: A mushroom is made up of many cells, so it is multicellular. Euglena, a bacterium and a diatom each have only one cell.
questions.lo: Classify organisms as unicellular or multicellular

notes.0: Euglena is made up of only one cell, so it is unicellular. Look for an organism made up of many cells.
notes.1: A bacterium is made up of only one cell, so it is unicellular. Look for an organism made up of many cells.
notes.3: A diatom is made up of only one cell, so it is unicellular. Look for an organism made up of many cells.

why.right: A mushroom is multicellular because it is made up of many cells.
wrong: A mushroom is multicellular because it is large enough to see without a microscope.
A mushroom is multicellular because it grows in damp places.

questions.q: A tiny worm is made of 300 cells. It is
choices: multicellular, because it has many cells
unicellular, because it is very light
questions.explain: The worm is made up of 300 cells, so it is multicellular. Being tiny does not matter, because it is the number of cells that counts.
questions.lo: Classify organisms as unicellular or multicellular

notes.1: Size does not decide whether an organism is unicellular. Count the cells in this worm.
notes.2: Mass does not decide whether an organism is unicellular. Count the cells in this worm.
notes.3: The worm is multicellular, but not because of its size. The question says it is tiny, so look for a better reason.

why.right: An organism is multicellular when it is made up of more than one cell, whatever its size.
wrong: An organism is multicellular when it is large enough to be seen without a microscope.
An organism is multicellular when it is heavy enough to weigh more than one gram.

questions.q: A diatom can only be seen under a microscope. It has one cell. It is
choices: unicellular, because it has one cell
multicellular, because it has a nucleus
questions.explain: The diatom has only one cell, so it is unicellular. Its small size is not the reason.
questions.lo: Classify organisms as unicellular or multicellular

notes.0: The diatom is unicellular, but size is not the reason. Some multicellular organisms are tiny too. Look at what the question says about its cells.
notes.2: Having a nucleus does not make an organism multicellular. Look at what the question says about the number of cells.
notes.3: All living things are alive, including unicellular ones. Look at what the question says about the number of cells.

why.right: An organism is unicellular when its whole body is made up of only one cell.
wrong: An organism is unicellular when it is small enough to need a microscope to be seen.
An organism is unicellular when it has no nucleus in its body.

questions.q: How can we tell if an organism is unicellular?
choices: measure the size of the organism
check if it lives in water
count the number of cells in it
questions.explain: An organism is unicellular if it has only one cell. Counting the cells, usually under a microscope, is the way to tell.
questions.lo: Classify organisms as unicellular or multicellular

notes.0: Some multicellular organisms are tiny, so size does not decide it. Think about what the word unicellular describes.
notes.1: Both unicellular and multicellular organisms can move. Think about what the word unicellular describes.
notes.2: Both unicellular and multicellular organisms live in water, such as bacteria and fish. Think about what the word unicellular describes.

why.right: Unicellular means made of one cell, so counting the cells is the only reliable test.
wrong: Unicellular means very small, so measuring the size is the only reliable test.
Unicellular means unable to move, so checking movement is the only reliable test.

questions.q: Which shows the correct order of organisation?
questions.explain: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form systems, and systems make up the organism.
questions.lo: Order the levels of organisation from cell to organism

notes.0: A system is made of organs, so organs must come before systems in the order. Check the order of the middle levels.
notes.1: Tissues are made of cells, so cells must come first. Check which level is the smallest.
notes.3: Organs are made of tissues, so tissues must come before organs. Check the order of the middle levels.

questions.q: In the levels of organisation, which level comes directly after tissue?
questions.explain: Different tissues work together to form an organ, so organ comes directly after tissue.
questions.lo: Order the levels of organisation from cell to organism

notes.0: A system is made of organs, so there is one level between tissue and system. Think about what tissues work together to form.
notes.1: The organism is the highest level, with two levels between it and tissue. Think about what tissues work together to form.
notes.2: Cells come before tissues, since tissues are made of cells. The question asks for the level after tissue.

questions.q: In the levels of organisation, which level comes directly after organ?
questions.explain: Organs work together to form a system, so system comes directly after organ.
questions.lo: Order the levels of organisation from cell to organism

notes.0: Tissues come before organs, since organs are made of tissues. The question asks for the level after organ.
notes.1: The cell is the lowest level and comes before organ. The question asks for the level after organ.
notes.3: The organism is the highest level, but there is one level between it and organ. Think about what organs work together to form.

questions.q: Cells that perform the same function work together to form a
questions.explain: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform the same function.
questions.lo: Order the levels of organisation from cell to organism

notes.0: An organ is made of different tissues working together. Think about the level formed directly by groups of similar cells.
notes.2: An organism is the whole living thing, made of many levels. Think about the level formed directly by groups of similar cells.
notes.3: A system is made of organs working together. Think about the level formed directly by groups of similar cells.

questions.q: Many organs working together to perform a function form a
questions.explain: A system is a group of organs that work together to perform a function, such as the digestive system.
questions.lo: Order the levels of organisation from cell to organism

notes.1: An organism is made up of several systems working together. Think about the level formed directly by groups of organs.
notes.2: A cell is the smallest level, not a group of organs. Think about the level formed directly by groups of organs.
notes.3: A tissue is a group of similar cells, which is below the level of organs. Think about the level formed directly by groups of organs.

questions.q: Different tissues work together to perform a function. What do they form?
questions.explain: An organ is made up of different tissues working together to perform a function, such as the heart or the stomach.
questions.lo: Order the levels of organisation from cell to organism

notes.0: A cell is the smallest level and cannot be made of tissues. Think about the level formed directly by different tissues.
notes.1: An organism is the whole living thing, several levels above tissue. Think about the level formed directly by different tissues.
notes.2: A system is made of organs, not directly of tissues. Think about the level formed directly by different tissues.

questions.q: The stomach is an example of
questions.explain: The stomach is made up of different tissues, such as muscle tissue, working together to digest food. So it is an organ.
questions.lo: Classify an example as a cell, tissue, organ, system or organism

notes.0: A tissue is a group of similar cells. The stomach contains several different tissues working together.
notes.1: The stomach is one part of the digestive system, not the whole system. A system has several organs.
notes.3: The stomach is made of a very large number of cells, not just one. Think about the level formed by several tissues together.

why.right: The stomach is an organ because it is made of different tissues working together to digest food.
wrong: The stomach is an organ because it is made of one type of cell doing one job.
The stomach is an organ because it carries out every life process for the body by itself.

questions.q: Blood in the human body is an example of
questions.explain: Blood is made up of groups of cells working together to carry out functions such as transporting substances. So it is a tissue.
questions.lo: Classify an example as a cell, tissue, organ, system or organism

notes.1: A system is made up of several organs. Blood is not made of organs. It is made of cells that work together.
notes.2: Blood contains a very large number of cells, not just one. Think about the level formed by groups of cells working together.
notes.3: An organ, such as the heart, is made of different tissues. Blood is made of cells working together, which is a lower level.

why.right: Blood is a tissue because it is a group of cells working together to perform a function.
wrong: Blood is a tissue because it is a liquid that fills all the organs of the body.
Blood is a tissue because it is made of one single large cell that flows around the body.

questions.q: A single root hair cell is an example of
questions.explain: A single root hair cell is one cell, so it is at the cell level of organisation.
questions.lo: Classify an example as a cell, tissue, organ, system or organism

notes.0: A tissue is a group of many similar cells. The question describes just one root hair cell.
notes.2: An organ such as the root is made of several tissues. The question describes just one root hair cell.
notes.3: A system is made of several organs. The question describes just one root hair cell.

questions.q: The root and stem working together to transport water form
questions.explain: The root and the stem are both organs. Organs working together to transport water form a system.
questions.lo: Classify an example as a cell, tissue, organ, system or organism

notes.0: A tissue is a group of similar cells. The root and the stem are each made of several tissues, so they are larger than a tissue.
notes.2: An organism is the whole plant, which also has leaves and flowers. Only the root and stem are named here.
notes.3: The root is one organ and the stem is another. Think about what organs working together form.

why.right: The root and stem form a system because they are organs working together to do one job.
wrong: The root and stem form a system because they are made of the same type of cell.
The root and stem form a system because together they make up the whole plant.

questions.q: The stem of a plant is an example of
questions.explain: The stem is made of different tissues, such as those that carry water and food, working together. So it is an organ.
questions.lo: Classify an example as a cell, tissue, organ, system or organism

notes.1: A tissue is a group of similar cells. The stem contains several different tissues working together.
notes.2: A stem is made of a very large number of cells, not one. Think about the level formed by several tissues.
notes.3: A system is made of several organs, such as the root and stem together. The stem on its own is only one part.

why.right: The stem is an organ because it is made of different tissues working together.
wrong: The stem is an organ because it is made of one tissue doing one job.
The stem is an organ because it can survive on its own as a whole living thing.

questions.q: A whole cat is an example of
questions.explain: A whole cat is a complete living thing made up of systems working together. So it is an organism, the highest level of organisation.
questions.lo: Classify an example as a cell, tissue, organ, system or organism

notes.0: An organ is one part of a body, such as the heart. A whole cat has many organs.
notes.1: A tissue is a group of similar cells. A whole cat is made of many different tissues.
notes.3: A system is a group of organs doing one job, such as the digestive system. A whole cat has many systems.

why.right: A whole cat is an organism because it is a complete living thing made of many systems.
wrong: A whole cat is an organism because it is a single system that does one job.
A whole cat is an organism because it is a group of similar cells.

questions.q: Different parts working together in a coordinated way to perform various functions is called
questions.explain: Division of labour is when different parts of an organism or a cell carry out different jobs and work together in a coordinated way.
questions.lo: Explain the division of labour in an organism and within a cell

notes.0: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants make food. It is one job, not the idea of parts sharing out jobs.
notes.1: Diffusion is the movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration. It is not about parts sharing out jobs.
notes.2: Pasteurisation is the heating of food such as milk to kill microorganisms. It is not about parts of an organism sharing out jobs.

questions.q: In a root hair cell, what does the cell wall do as water enters?
questions.explain: As water enters, the cell swells. The tough, rigid cell wall stops it swelling too much, which prevents the cell from bursting.
questions.lo: Explain the division of labour in an organism and within a cell

notes.0: Controlling what enters and leaves the cell is the job of the cell membrane. The cell wall is tough and rigid, so think about what it resists.
notes.1: Storing substances is the job of the vacuole. The cell wall is tough and rigid, so think about what it does as the cell fills with water.
notes.3: Making food is the job of chloroplasts, and root hair cells have none. Think about what a tough, rigid wall does as the cell fills with water.

why.right: The rigid cell wall stops the cell swelling too much, so the cell cannot burst.
wrong: The cell wall controls how much water enters, so the cell cannot burst.
The cell wall stores the extra water, so the cell cannot burst.

questions.q: Why can the vacuole not take over the job of the chloroplast?
choices: each part has its own specific function
questions.explain: Each part of a cell has its own structure suited to its own job. The vacuole has no chlorophyll, so it cannot carry out photosynthesis like the chloroplast.
questions.lo: Explain the division of labour in an organism and within a cell

notes.0: Storing waste is the job of the vacuole, not the chloroplast. Think about whether each part can do the job of another.
notes.2: Plant cells do have vacuoles, often a large central one. Think about whether each part can do the job of another.
notes.3: Size is not the reason. A plant cell vacuole is often large. Think about whether each part is suited to the job of another.

why.right: The vacuole cannot do the job of the chloroplast because it has no chlorophyll to absorb light.
wrong: The vacuole cannot do the job of the chloroplast because it is full of waste and has no space.
The vacuole cannot do the job of the chloroplast because it is found only in animal cells.
